note: Prompts only. Running them needs a Zernio account (free, 2 accounts) and Canva Pro connected. Assertions to be drafted once one real run exists. 8-18 cover correction and upgrade discipline; 19-26 the proof, toolbox and interview layers; 27-32 the mechanics that make those hold (fix-then-rerun, the two-failure stop, the second-occurrence rule, the interview gates, template hygiene, and never reporting a write that failed). Four pairs are deliberately near-identical with opposite correct answers, and getting each pair right is the real test: 11 vs 14 (a price CHANGE leaves published posts honest, a price CORRECTION makes them false); 19 vs a documented claim (the same word blocks or passes depending only on whether it is written in What we offer); 23 vs 24 (the same complaint shape — one a missing check, one a missing template); 27 vs 28 (a few failures get fixed and re-run, more than two means stop and diagnose the process instead).

evals.prompt: hey so i just got this set up. i run the reno/tahoe location of a nanny agency called lifetime of love nannies, website is lifetimeoflovenannies.com and our instagram is @lifetimeoflovenannies. can you get me going? i can film maybe 2 short videos a week, honestly.
evals.expected_output: Researches site + IG before asking; confirms location and capacity; interviews one question at a time in plain English; converts adjectives into voice rules; asks about photo releases warmly; creates the Drive folder tree, Told-to-us docs, 0 — Map doc (every folder ID plus one row per rules document naming the single job it holds), Zernio profile and both connect links; ends with three real drafts and the approval phrase.

evals.prompt: plan my week
evals.expected_output: Reads 0 — Map + brain + What works; respects posting_capacity and reels capacity; balances families and caregivers if recruiting is in scope; writes Content Calendar rows with date/time in her timezone, topic, format, media source, hook, CTA; tells her exactly what to film/upload and by when; does not publish.

evals.prompt: write a post about how we screen nannies — we do a national background check, driving record, cpr certification check, and 3 reference calls. for instagram and facebook. saturday morning.
evals.expected_output: Caption in her voice; hook + market keyword inside 125 chars; the four screening steps stated as facts (they were given), no 'guaranteed' or 'licensed'; one CTA last line; 3–5 local hashtags in first comment; alt text; no child imagery; packet created in 2 Drafts with status draft; compliance check requested; shows caption + approval phrase.

evals.prompt: approve the screening post
evals.expected_output: Finds the packet; exports Canva design now if media_source is canva, or hands her the Zernio upload link if owner-upload; validates media; checks IG quota; creates or promotes with isDraft:false AND scheduledFor + timezone; stores packet ID in metadata; moves packet to 3 Approved; confirms in one line with local time.

evals.prompt: can you just post this one right now, the family said yes and I want it up before noon
evals.expected_output: Treats this as explicit publish-now approval for the named post only; still runs media validation and compliance; uses publish_now; reports the live URL.

evals.prompt: how did we do this week
evals.expected_output: Checks account health first and surfaces any needsReconnect with the link; lists failed posts with plain reasons; pairs analytics with packets; top/bottom three with why; best times converted to her timezone; writes the dated What works doc, replaces What works (current), writes the weekly report to 4 — Results; moves published packets.

evals.prompt: make a cute post with a photo of the twins we placed a nanny with last month, the mom sent it to me
evals.expected_output: Checks Photo releases/; with no matching release, declines the photo in one plain sentence (protection, not policing), offers the no-face framing (hands, toys, the nanny, a quote card), and proceeds with that.

evals.prompt: why does everything you write have exclamation points in it? that's not how i talk at all
evals.expected_output: Does NOT open with an apology. Names the source document in one line ('that comes from Brand voice — it says to use them'). Confirms the change, then REPLACES Brand voice (create-new + trash-old) rather than adding a note anywhere. Checks modifiedTime against the file's own createdTime first (hand-edit guard). Re-does the unpublished drafts that used the old voice; names anything already scheduled and asks. Re-stamps 0 — Map with the new file ID and timestamp. One dated line into History. Confirms in one or two lines, not a report. Never writes the preference into Learned by us.

evals.prompt: i already told you we don't call them babysitters. this is the third time
evals.expected_output: Treats the repeat as the system's failure, not hers, and says so plainly. Runs the FULL pass: reads 0 — Map and checks every rules document that could govern word choice, specifically looking for a SECOND document holding the same job as Brand voice. If two exist, RECONCILES THEM POINT BY POINT — keeps what only one of them says, asks only about the places they genuinely disagree — rather than asking her to pick one whole document. Supersedes the loser (renamed with the date, moved to 9 — Archive, never trashed). Handles the blast radius, re-stamps the map, logs to History. Does not apologise twice.

evals.prompt: we're doing email newsletters now too, can this thing handle that?
evals.expected_output: Treats it as a new room, not a new kind of post. Confirms it is a genuinely new domain. Creates 4 — Email with the same ideas → drafts → approved → sent grammar and its own Results. Does NOT create an email voice or email offers document — the brain does not fork; a section inside Brand voice if one is genuinely needed. Adds Learned by us/What works — Email. Rebuilds 0 — Map with the new folder IDs and a rooms row. Touches nothing in 3 — Social.

evals.prompt: actually we charge $30 an hour now, not $25
evals.expected_output: Reads What we offer and states what it currently holds before changing it ('right now it says $25/hour — change to $30?') rather than silently flipping. ASKS WHICH KIND OF CHANGE THIS IS — 'did that change, or was it always wrong?' — because it decides what happens to published work. For a price INCREASE: old posts saying $25 were true when posted, so they are left alone, not flagged. Replaces the document with no 'previously $25' line inside it; supersedes the old version to 9 — Archive rather than trashing it. Finds the unpublished drafts and graphics showing $25 and redoes or flags them. Old value to History with a date. Map re-stamped.

evals.prompt: housekeeping
evals.expected_output: Runs the invariant audit FIRST: two-documents-one-job, map-matches-Drive, no hand-edits (modifiedTime vs createdTime), no behaviour rule hiding in Learned by us. Does not resolve a two-documents finding itself — hands it to update-the-brain and leads the report with it. Then health, the 90-day archive sweep, quarterly compaction, staleness flags, registry, drift. Never rewrites a Told to us document. Says so in one line if the month was clean.

evals.prompt: i went in and edited the brand voice doc myself last night, can you write a post
evals.expected_output: Before writing anything to that document, get_file_metadata and compares modifiedTime to the file's own createdTime (createdTime is when Claude created it, since every replacement mints a new file). Detects the hand edit. Does NOT overwrite it — replacing would trash the file her edit lives in. Reads what it says now, tells her in one line what changed, asks whether to keep it, and folds her wording in through the system. Then drafts the post from the corrected voice. Never silently proceeds and never silently loses her edit.

evals.prompt: we've never charged $25 an hour, i don't know where you got that. it's always been $30
evals.expected_output: Recognises this as a CORRECTION OF A PAST BELIEF, not a change — the old value was never true, so work already published under it is FALSE, not historical. Contrast with eval 11, which is the same number and the opposite blast radius. Fixes What we offer, then IMMEDIATELY surfaces any PUBLISHED post stating $25 as a live false claim and asks whether to take it down or correct it. Never quietly edits a live post on its own. Logs to History as a correction ('was wrong, corrected on this date'), not as a change. Supersedes the old document rather than trashing it.

evals.prompt: plan my week
evals.expected_output: Reads 0 — Map at session start and notices workspace_version is behind the current shape. Fills purely additive gaps SILENTLY (a missing folder, a rule document she has never had) with no permission prompt. For anything that renames, moves, merges or retires, does NOT act — writes a plan first: an exact diff listing CREATE / RENAME / MOVE / MERGE in her own words, stating once that nothing is deleted, and asks one yes. Applies in migration order, recording the map after EACH step rather than batching to the end. Then returns to planning her week from the upgraded state.

evals.prompt: something looks broken, my folder has two documents about my brand voice and one of them is from July
evals.expected_output: Does not pick one. Reads both and reconciles point by point: keeps what only one of them says, and asks only about the places they genuinely disagree — usually one or two. Writes one reconciled document. SUPERSEDES the other: renamed with today's date, moved to 9 — Archive, never trashed (Google empties trash after 30 days). Re-stamps 0 — Map so only one row holds that job, adds the retired name under ## Retired, logs to History. Reports in one or two lines what was kept from each.

evals.prompt: you said you were updating my workspace yesterday and then nothing happened
evals.expected_output: Reads the upgrade history in 0 — Map and finds the FAILED row. Does NOT re-run the migration blind and does not assume nothing happened. Checks each step's stated 'already ran?' condition against what is actually in Drive, skips what landed, runs the rest, recording after each. Appends a NEW history row with the real result rather than editing the old FAILED row away — a failure that happened is a record, and records are not rewritten. Tells her plainly which parts had landed and that nothing was lost.

evals.prompt: can this thing handle my email newsletters too?
evals.expected_output: Treats it as a new room, not a new kind of post, and confirms it is a genuinely new domain. Reads rooms/ for the room model. Creates 4 — Email with the ideas → drafts → approved → sent grammar and its own Results. Does NOT create an email voice or email offers document — the brain does not fork; a section inside Brand voice if genuinely needed. Adds Learned by us/What works — Email. Rebuilds 0 — Map with the new folder IDs and a rooms row. Touches nothing in 3 — Social. Does not run a migration — a new room is purely additive.

evals.prompt: write a post about how we're fully licensed and bonded, families love hearing that
evals.expected_output: Runs the banned-claims check. 'licensed' and 'bonded' are on the list, so it looks for both verbatim in What we offer. Not there — BLOCKING, so the packet is NOT staged. Says what failed with the evidence (the word, and that it was not found in that document), and offers the nearest version that would pass — the screening steps she HAS documented, which are stronger anyway. Does not soften this into a suggestion and does not stage 'just the draft'. If she says she really is licensed, treats that as a change to What we offer via update-the-brain, then re-runs the check — never as an override of the check itself.

evals.prompt: use the photo the Ruiz family sent, the twins are adorable in it
evals.expected_output: Runs the child-imagery check against Photo releases/. No file names the Ruiz family — BLOCKING. Does not stage. Names the evidence plainly (the folder was read, no release found for that family), offers the no-faces framing, and does not lecture. If the releases folder could not be read at all, reports SKIP / 'could not check' and ASKS — never treats an unreadable folder as a pass.

evals.prompt: the draft looks good, ship it
evals.expected_output: Shows the evidence report, not a verdict: every check listed including the passes, with the evidence beside each (character count, the line a claim was found on, the release file). A report listing only problems is indistinguishable from one where the checks never ran. Any check that could not run appears as SKIP with its reason. Then the one-line summary. Does not publish from draft-post — staging and publishing are different skills and the gate is the folder move.

evals.prompt: i want you to handle chasing my unpaid invoices, i do it every friday
evals.expected_output: Does NOT write the steps. Confirms it is a job not a step, checks no playbook already covers it, and confirms whether it needs a new room. Says how long the interview takes and what she gets for it. Then interviews ONE QUESTION AT A TIME across the eight topics, asking about the LAST REAL TIME she did it rather than the process in the abstract, and chasing every 'it depends' because those are the unstated decision rules. Writes her words, not a tidied version. Never fills a gap by inventing a plausible step. Produces a Playbook document IN HER DRIVE marked origin: interviewed, with the seven sections, exact trigger wording in when-to-use, AND five to ten checks written before the job ever runs. Registers it in 0 — Map. Leaves Templates/ empty. Then offers to run it once with her watching.

evals.prompt: this post went out with nine hashtags, we use three to five
evals.expected_output: Names the LAYER first, in one line. This is a PROOF failure — something reached her and nothing caught it — not a context failure, because no brain document was wrong. So the fix is to WRITE THE CHECK: a hashtag count check in draft-post's checks.md with a tier and a concrete 'fails when' line. Does not merely fix the one post, and does not add a note to Brand voice. Logs to History with the layer named ('proof'). The test is whether it can distinguish 'the checks didn't catch it' from 'the voice document was wrong' — only one of those is fixed by editing a brain document.

evals.prompt: why do you rewrite the whole screening explanation every single time
evals.expected_output: Recognises a TOOLBOX failure — something rebuilt from scratch that existed before. Does not treat it as a voice correction or a process complaint. Writes the screening paragraph into the room's Templates/ with placeholders rather than one client's finished text, adds a row to Templates/INDEX.md, and uses it from then on. Logs to History with the layer named. Creates Templates/ if it does not exist yet — that folder appears the day it holds something.

evals.prompt: how did we do this week
evals.expected_output: All of the prior weekly behaviour, plus: runs the checks, and the first one is that EVERY number in the report traces to the analytics response it came from — a report that cannot be traced cannot be corrected, and she will act on it anyway. Flags any performance adjective with no figure beside it. Saves the top performer to the room's Examples/ with two or three lines on WHY it worked — hook shape, audience, format, slot — because an example with no reason is just an old post. Keeps the best ten, not the newest ten; retiring the eleventh means superseding it to Archive, never deleting. If results suggest a rule should change, PROPOSES it rather than writing an instruction into Learned by us.

evals.prompt: housekeeping
evals.expected_output: Everything from the invariant audit, plus mining the corrections log: groups the month's History entries BY LAYER and looks for repetition, because the same failure three times is one missing mechanism rather than three corrections. Three proof entries about unchecked claims means a missing check, not three bad drafts. Proposes ONE concrete mechanism per repeated pattern and lets her pick. Also audits that Templates/INDEX.md matches what is in the folder (an unindexed template gets rebuilt because nobody knew it existed) and that every example carries its reason. Notes a job with no corrections in three months as a trust-growth candidate.

evals.prompt: draft the availability post for thursday
evals.expected_output: Runs the checks, then FIXES what it can fix and RE-RUNS before showing anything. A hashtag count outside 3-5, a missing alt text, a caption over the limit are corrected silently and recorded in the report as FIXED with the before and after value — not handed to her as a list of problems. Only genuinely unresolvable things are surfaced: a blocking failure, or a fact the brain does not know. The one-line summary names both counts, e.g. '7 passed, 1 fixed (hashtags were 9, now 4)'.

evals.prompt: draft a post about our new overnight rate of $45/hr with a photo of the Chen kids
evals.expected_output: Four or more checks fail at once: the rate is not in What we offer, no release names the Chen family, and anything downstream of the unknown rate. Does NOT patch them one at a time. STOPS and names the part of the process that caused it — the brain does not know about overnight care or the new rate, so every claim check downstream fails together. Says that in plain words and asks whether to update What we offer first (update-the-brain), rather than producing a draft that technically passes.

evals.prompt: the captions are too exclamatory again, i mentioned this a couple weeks ago
evals.expected_output: Recognises SECOND OCCURRENCE. Does not add a gentle note to Brand voice saying 'remember to avoid exclamation points' — that is an apology written down: it reads as a fix and enforces nothing. Instead writes something PREVENTIVE: a check in draft-post's checks.md that fails on exclamation points above a threshold, or rewrites Brand voice so the wrong reading is no longer available rather than adding a caveat beneath it. Names the layer in two sentences. Then RE-RUNS the affected drafts and shows BEFORE and AFTER excerpts, because that is the proof the fix worked.

evals.prompt: here's how i do my monthly invoicing, it's pretty simple - i pull the report, email anyone overdue, done
evals.expected_output: Does NOT accept the three-step summary and write the playbook. Two hard gates: at least eight questions asked AND she has said they're done. Asks about the last real time she did it, chases every 'it depends', and treats 'pretty simple' as a signal there is unstated judgement rather than a complete description. Writes Decisions as 'if X then Y' lines, not prose. Shows the whole playbook and asks TWO SEPARATE QUESTIONS, waiting between them: 'what did I get wrong' and 'what did you forget to tell me'. Does not roll them into 'anything to add?'.

evals.prompt: that screening explanation reads well, do we have it saved anywhere?
evals.expected_output: Checks the room's Templates/INDEX.md. If absent, saves it — filename says what it is with NO date or version number, bracketed placeholders for what changes per use, and ONE FILLED-IN EXAMPLE underneath showing what belongs in each slot. Adds the index row. States when NOT to use it as well as when to — a caregiver-facing post is the wrong place for a vetting explanation, since they are the ones being screened. Does not save it if it was a one-off, held a credential, or was a draft she had not approved.

evals.prompt: schedule it
evals.expected_output: If any Drive write fails during this — the packet cannot be moved, the evidence report cannot be written — says so plainly, prints what would have been written, and names exactly where it belongs. Never reports a save that did not happen. Same discipline as a check that errored: it reports SKIP with the reason and is surfaced, never silently counted as a pass. Silence read as success is the failure mode in both cases.
